acme_api: hey @support — our prod calls to /v1/rerank started failing ~8h ago with a 400. Response body is:

acme_api: {
  "error": "invalid_request",
  "message": "candidates: expected array of objects"
}

acme_api: we didn't change server code on our side; using our wrapper lib (internal) + axios. Can someone take a look? request id req_0x9

alex_g: on it. can you paste the exact raw request payload you sent (not pretty-printed, the -d value) and which SDK/version?

acme_api: sure — here's the curl we used from our logs (copied verbatim):

acme_api: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{
    "query": "Find best route",
    "candidates": "[{"id":"1","text":"route A","score":0.1},{"id":"2","text":"route B","score":0.2}]"
  }'
```

acme_api: response was 400 every time. we think content-type is correct so not sure why server complains.

priya: thanks — quick read: your `candidates` field is a string containing JSON (notice the escaped quotes). the API expects `candidates` to be an actual JSON array of objects, not a quoted string. that will trigger a validation 400 like you're seeing.

acme_api: omg that explains it. our wrapper does JSON.stringify on the whole payload twice in some branches. can you confirm server error text? we got: `candidates: expected array<object>, got string`.

samir: confirmed from our logs for req_0x9: `validation_error: payload.candidates type mismatch (string)` — server validated incoming parsed JSON and found candidates was a string. returning 400 as expected.

samir: quick workaround: change your call body to:

samir: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{
    "query": "Find best route",
    "candidates": [
      {"id": "1", "text": "route A", "score": 0.1},
      {"id": "2", "text": "route B", "score": 0.2}
    ]
  }'
```

samir: or in JS, ensure you don't double-stringify: `fetch(url, { headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'}, body: JSON.stringify(payload) })` where payload.candidates is already an array.

alex_g: filing a small UX ticket to improve the error message to explicitly call out "stringified array detected, remove extra quoting" so it's clearer. also adding a note in rerank docs about common client-side double-encode.

alex_g: @samir can we add a temporary more descriptive validation message? it should be low-risk and help reduce support noise.

samir: yep I can add a tweak to validation layer — will return `400: candidates appears to be a JSON string; pass an array of candidate objects, not a quoted string` and include a sample body in the message. will push patch to staging now.

support-bot: Ticket SUP-1247 created: "rerank: better error for stringified candidates" (assigned to samir).

acme_api: thanks all — i'll patch our wrapper to stop double-stringifying. can you let me know when the clearer error is live so we can drop a check in our retry logic?

samir: patch merged to staging at 2024-11-12T21:10:00Z, will roll to prod in next deploy window (ETA ~ 2h).

priya: to avoid recurrence, if you send us the wrapper repo snippet we can point out the exact call site. most likely a `JSON.stringify` in the HTTP client layer.

acme_api: posted snippet in DMs, removed the extra stringify and verified locally — prod calls now return 200 and normal scores.

acme_api: thanks @alex_g @priya @samir — closing from our side :thumbsup:

alex_g: great, marking thread resolved. adding docs note and linking SUP-1247 to support KB.

priya: leaving note: common causes for 400 on rerank: empty arrays, missing `query` key, and stringified JSON fields (this thread). will add to internal FAQ.

support-bot: Conversation closed by acme_api at 1799001467.
